lines.trans: Every good neighbourhood café needs one hot lunch bowl and one signature cake.
Did we just get promoted to official taste testers, Hao?

lines.trans: Best job in the building! Which bowl do we try first, Mei?
Left spoon: roasted tomato soup with fresh courtyard herbs.
Rich, warm, and great with crusty bread on a rainy afternoon!
Right spoon: golden lentil soup with lemon and olive oil—even better!
Now try the two lemon tart slices: thin pastry on the left, almond crust on the right.
Oh—the almond crust with Saturday market lemon is unbeatable!
Save one slice for Chen, Mei, or he will lock us out of the kitchen!
So Wednesday's menu is set: golden lentil soup, warm bread, almond lemon tart, and tea!
Simple, honest, and easy to serve quickly from noon to evening.
Now let us hope for sunny skies tomorrow so our shutter paint dries!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yī. Changes tone to yí before 4th tone (一个 yí gè) and yì before 1st/2nd/3rd tones (一杯 yì bēi).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shàng. Used both as a directional verb/complement ('up, onto') and location word ('on top of').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shàng zhuō. Verb-object compound 上 ('go onto') + 桌 ('table'): used for dishes brought out ready to eat.

examples.text: 热汤一做好就可以马上端上桌。
examples.trans: As soon as the hot soup is ready, it can be served onto the table right away.

examples.text: 刚出炉的热面包很快就上桌了。
examples.trans: The freshly baked warm bread was soon brought to the table.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià wǔ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个下午 ('an afternoon').

examples.text: 您尽管看，宋老师。星期一下午大堂暗。
examples.trans: Go right ahead, Teacher Song. Monday afternoon the lobby was dim.

examples.text: 先别对外面透露一个字！让两兄弟先过完这个星期五下午！
examples.trans: Not a single word to anyone outside yet! Let the two brothers have their Friday afternoon first!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià yǔ. Literally 'fall rain'; Mandarin expresses weather with verb + weather noun.

examples.text: 下雨的时候，纸不会弄丢房间名单。
examples.trans: When it rains, paper will not lose the room list.

examples.text: 每次弹完琴，他都问为什么下雨天钢琴声音更暖。
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, he asked why the piano sounded warmer on rainy days.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bù rán. Links a warning or alternative ('otherwise…').

examples.text: 快去跟他聊聊，小晴，不然木地板都要踩破了！
examples.trans: Go talk to him quickly, Qing, or he will wear right through the wooden floorboards!

examples.text: 快带上雨伞吧，不然会淋湿的。
examples.trans: Bring an umbrella quickly, otherwise you will get soaked.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎng. Used instead of 二 when counting things with a measure word (两个, 两把, 两间).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gè. Most common Mandarin measure word (量词), placed between a number/demonstrative and a noun (一个人, 这个).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhōng wǔ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个中午 ('a noon hour').

examples.text: 先生？他说：请别打开白纸包，我星期五中午来。
examples.trans: Sir? He says: Please do not open the white paper parcel; I will come Friday at noon.

examples.text: 等星期五中午箱子主人进来，我一定坐第一排看！
examples.trans: When the suitcase owner walks in Friday at noon, I am sitting in the front row!

meanings.note: Pinyin: le. After a verb, marks completion; at the end of a sentence, signals a change of situation.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cóng. Marks a starting point in space or time (从早上到晚上 'from morning to night').

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: 从这儿往里走。我帮您把蓝色行李箱提上去。
examples.trans: Walk inward from here. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tā. Third-person singular masculine pronoun; pronounced identically to 她 and 它.

examples.text: 他没要回那个装木头小火车的箱子吗？
examples.trans: Did he not ask back for that case with the wooden train?

examples.text: 他留了纸条，请我们保管到星期五。
examples.trans: He left a note asking us to keep it until Friday.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎ. Colloquial fusion of 两个, never followed by 个 (我们俩 'the two of us').

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

examples.text: 别动，你们俩。听到路边汽车停下的声音了吗？
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you. Hear that car engine stopping at the curb?

meanings.note: Pinyin: bàng wǎn. Combines 傍 ('draw near to') + 晚 ('evening'): the golden hour around sunset.

examples.text: 傍晚的时候，院子里的灯笼一盏接一盏亮了。
examples.trans: At dusk, the lanterns in the courtyard lit up one after another.

examples.text: 夏天的傍晚最适合坐在院子里乘凉。
examples.trans: Summer evenings at dusk are perfect for sitting in the courtyard to enjoy the breeze.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiān. Placed before the verb to sequence actions: 先…再… ('first…, then…').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: quán. Emphasizes entirety before 都 or a verb (全都 'every single one').

examples.text: 怪不得这么重，全是木头和皮鞋！
examples.trans: No wonder it was so heavy—all wood and leather shoes!

examples.text: 四张桌子，八把椅子，全摆好了！
examples.trans: Four tables, eight chairs—everything is set in place!

meanings.note: Pinyin: gāng. Placed right before a verb to show the action happened moments ago.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

examples.text: 一到七号钥匙全拿走了，八号房刚刷了油漆。
examples.trans: Every key from one to seven is taken, and room eight just got fresh paint.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dào. Works as main verb ('arrive') or result complement ('succeed in reaching/perceiving', 找到, 听到).

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房今天到。
examples.trans: Right, eight guest rooms, eight brass keys. Room four arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiā. Used for adding sugar, milk, or extra items (加糖 'add sugar').

examples.text: 请给我不加糖的红茶，再来一片热面包。
examples.trans: Black tea without added sugar, please, and one slice of warm bread.

examples.text: 太好了！请加牛奶和一点糖。
examples.trans: Wonderful! With milk and a little sugar, please.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sháo. Used both as a noun (勺子 'spoon') and as a measure word for spoonfuls (一勺蜂蜜 'a spoonful of honey').

examples.text: 喝热柠檬茶的时候，加一勺蜂蜜最香。
examples.trans: Hot lemon tea smells best when you add a spoonful of honey.

examples.text: 请给我拿一把干净的小木勺。
examples.trans: Please bring me a clean little wooden spoon.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shēng zhí. Separable verb-object compound 升 ('rise/promote') + 职 ('post/rank').

examples.text: 哥哥上个月刚升职，请全家人吃了一顿晚饭。
examples.trans: My older brother just got promoted last month and treated the whole family to dinner.

examples.text: 她工作认真负责，很快就升职了。
examples.trans: She works conscientiously and was promoted before long.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǔ cān. Combines 午 ('noon') + 餐 ('meal'); slightly more formal/menu-friendly than 午饭.

examples.text: 咖啡角每天中午提供热汤和面包做午餐。
examples.trans: Every day at noon the café corner serves hot soup and bread for lunch.

examples.text: 我们星期天中午一起吃顿简单的午餐吧。
examples.trans: Let's have a simple lunch together at noon on Sunday.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chú fáng. Measure word (量词): 间 (jiān), e.g. 一间厨房 ('a kitchen').

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

examples.text: 糟了！周经理，小晴，厨房出急事了！
examples.trans: Oh no! Manager Zhou, Qing, we have a kitchen emergency!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòu. Marks an action repeating, or pairs two qualities in 又A又B ('both A and B').

examples.text: 真的可以吗？看着又好看又暖和！
examples.trans: Is that really alright? It looks both lovely and warm!

examples.text: 又是深蓝色行李箱！这是宋老师的吗？
examples.trans: Another dark-blue suitcase! Is this Teacher Song's?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǐ. Read zhǐ as the adverb 'only' before verbs, and zhī as a measure word for cups, boxes, and small animals.

examples.text: 而且他坐晚上八点的火车到——只剩四十分钟了！
examples.trans: And he arrives on the eight o'clock evening train—only forty minutes left!

examples.text: 只剩三十五分钟了！他肯定会写一星差评！
examples.trans: Only thirty-five minutes left! He will surely write a one-star bad review!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòu bian. Measure word (量词): 边 (biān), e.g. 右边 ('the right side').

examples.text: 这面圆镜子挂哪儿？窗户左边还是右边？
examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror? Left of the window or right?

examples.text: 挂在书桌右边吧，那里光线好。
examples.trans: Hang it to the right of the desk, where the light is good.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ba. At the end of a sentence, softens commands into friendly suggestions ('let's…') or asks for confirmation.

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hé. Joins nouns or pronouns ('A and B'), NEVER two whole clauses; also means 'with' (和你一样).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: kā fēi guǎn. Measure word (量词): 家 (jiā), e.g. 一家咖啡馆 ('a café').

examples.text: 每天服务街坊邻居——就像对公众开放的早间咖啡馆？！
examples.trans: Serves neighbours daily—like a morning café open to the public?!

examples.text: 比现在翻一倍！我们真的要对整条街开放小院咖啡馆吗？
examples.trans: Double what I bake now! Are we really opening the courtyard café to our whole street?

meanings.note: Pinyin: wā. Expresses admiration or delight.

examples.text: 哇，看这间房！大木头房梁，窗户正对着院子！
examples.trans: Wow, look at this room! Big wooden beams, and a window facing the courtyard!

examples.text: 插上老陈的铜台灯……哇，黄色灯光真暖和！
examples.trans: Plug in Chen's brass lamp... wow, how warm that yellow light is!

meanings.note: Pinyin: nǎ. Combines with a measure word to ask 'which?' (哪个 'which one?', 哪间 'which room?').

examples.text: 等一下，小晴……你拿了哪一包黄油？
examples.trans: Wait a second, Qing... which packet of butter did you grab?

examples.text: 对！左边有两条小路——我走哪一条？
examples.trans: Yes! There are two small lanes on the left—which one do I take?

meanings.note: Pinyin: huí tóu. Appears in the friendly farewell 回头见！ ('See you soon!').

examples.text: 我先去送热茶，我们回头聊！
examples.trans: Let me deliver this hot tea first—we will talk soon!

examples.text: 今天辛苦了，回头见！
examples.trans: Great work today—see you soon!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. As main verb/preposition, gives location (在院子里); before another verb, marks ongoing action ('be doing').

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wài mian. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 外面世界 ('the outside').

examples.text: 外面一模一样，可是你看里面！
examples.trans: The outside is identical, yet look inside!

examples.text: 外面下着大雨，街上酒店全满了！我们怎么办？
examples.trans: It is pouring rain outside and every hotel on the street is full! What do we do?

meanings.note: Pinyin: dà. Everyday adjective for size, age, and strong wind or rain.

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 两双棕色大男鞋，还有灰色毛衣。
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes, plus grey sweaters.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tài. Often frames 太 + adj + 了 for warm exclamations (太好了！ 'Wonderful!').

examples.text: 太好了。请告诉我需要知道什么。
examples.trans: Great. Please tell me what I need to know.

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

meanings.note: Pinyin: hǎo. Main adjective 'good'; as a result complement after a verb, means 'ready/completed properly' (修好, 准备好).

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hǎo hē. Combines 好 ('good/pleasant to') + 喝 ('drink'), parallel to 好吃 ('tasty to eat').

examples.text: 加了柠檬汁的金黄扁豆汤特别好喝。
examples.trans: The golden lentil soup with lemon juice added is especially delicious.

examples.text: 小美泡的热薄荷茶清香好喝。
examples.trans: The hot mint tea Mei steeped is fragrant and delicious.

好让.gloss: so that; in order to let

meanings.en: so that; in order to let
meanings.note: Pinyin: hǎo ràng. Purpose conjunction introducing the desired result in the second clause.

examples.text: 把窗户打开吧，好让新鲜空气吹进来。
examples.trans: Open the window so that fresh air can blow in.

examples.text: 希望明天出太阳，好让木板上的新油漆快点干透。
examples.trans: Let's hope the sun comes out tomorrow so that the fresh paint on the boards dries quickly.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dìng hǎo. Resultative compound 定 ('decide/fix') + 好 ('settled/complete').

examples.text: 星期三咖啡角的菜单已经全部定好了。
examples.trans: Wednesday's menu for the café corner is now completely set.

examples.text: 我们定好了明天早上八点一起刷窗板。
examples.trans: We set eight o'clock tomorrow morning to paint the shutters together.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shí zài. Describes sturdy materials, unpretentious food, or dependable people.

examples.text: 钢琴里面全是实在的木头、毛毡和钢丝。
examples.trans: Inside a piano it is all solid wood, felt, and steel wire.

examples.text: 这碗热扁豆汤用料实在，喝一碗就饱了。
examples.trans: This bowl of hot lentil soup is made with hearty ingredients; one bowl fills you right up.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kè zhàn. Measure word (量词): 家 (jiā), e.g. 一家客栈 ('an inn').

examples.text: 还没有吗？请记下我们客栈的电话和地址，谢谢！
examples.trans: Not yet? Please write down our inn's phone number and address, thank you!

examples.text: 我们客栈都是五星级服务……哎呀！
examples.trans: At our inn, everything is five-star service... whoops!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiā. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个家 ('a home').

examples.text: 上面怎么用铅笔整齐画了这条街三家客栈？
examples.trans: Why are three inns on this street neatly sketched in pencil on it?

examples.text: 看我们这家旁边写着：院子宽度、街道声音、安静九分！
examples.trans: Look beside ours: Courtyard width, street noise, quiet score nine points!

meanings.note: Pinyin: cháng. Specifically tasting food or drink (尝一尝 / 尝一下); contrast 试 ('try out' objects or clothes).

examples.text: 快来尝一口刚出炉的热面包！
examples.trans: Come taste a bite of warm bread fresh from the oven!

examples.text: 卖蜂蜜的大姐请我们尝了一小勺山蜂蜜。
examples.trans: The honey vendor invited us to taste a little spoonful of mountain honey.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cháng chang. Softened reduplication of 尝 ('taste'), standard when inviting someone to sample food.

examples.text: 快来尝尝我刚烤出来的杏仁柠檬挞！
examples.trans: Come have a taste of the almond lemon tart I just baked!

examples.text: 你先尝尝这碗番茄汤咸淡合适不合适。
examples.trans: Have a taste of this tomato soup first to see if the seasoning is right.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gōng zuò. Measure word (量词): 份 (fèn), e.g. 一份工作 ('a job').

examples.text: 我只是检查安全。这是我的工作。
examples.trans: I am simply checking security. That is my job.

examples.text: 一点也不介意！窗下这张宽书桌正适合我工作。
examples.trans: Not at all! And this wide desk beneath the window suits my work ideally.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuǒ bian. Measure word (量词): 边 (biān), e.g. 左边 ('the left side').

examples.text: 这面圆镜子挂哪儿？窗户左边还是右边？
examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror? Left of the window or right?

examples.text: 对！左边有两条小路——我走哪一条？
examples.trans: Yes! There are two small lanes on the left—which one do I take?

meanings.note: Pinyin: xī wàng. Works as both verb ('hope that…') and noun ('hope').

examples.text: 周经理的意思是……希望每位客人都觉得有十分满意！
examples.trans: What Manager Zhou means is... we hope every guest feels ten-out-of-ten satisfied!

examples.text: 希望您今晚在我们客栈睡个好觉。
examples.trans: We hope you sleep soundly at our inn tonight.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gān tòu. Resultative compound 干 (gān, 'dry') + 透 ('thoroughly / all the way through').

examples.text: 要等第一层绿油漆完全干透，才能刷第二层。
examples.trans: You have to wait until the first coat of green paint dries completely before brushing on the second.

examples.text: 姑姑把九号房锁上，想等屋顶先干透。
examples.trans: My aunt locked Room Nine, wanting to wait until the roof dried completely.

当上.gloss: become; take up a post or role

meanings.en: become; take up a post or role
meanings.note: Pinyin: dāng shàng. Resultative compound 当 ('serve as') + 上 ('attain a role').

examples.text: 志鹏笑着说他们兄弟俩当上了正式试吃员。
examples.trans: Peng joked that the two brothers had become official taste testers.

examples.text: 苦练三年以后，她终于当上了乐团的首席乐手。
examples.trans: After three years of dedicated practice, she finally became first chair in the orchestra.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hěn. Links a subject to a simple predicate adjective without needing 是 (今天很冷 'It is cold today').

examples.text: 你好，小美，很高兴认识你！好香啊！
examples.trans: Hello, Mei, nice to meet you! Something smells wonderful!

examples.text: 没错！你已经很习惯这儿了。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in here.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kuài. As an adjective/adverb, 'fast/quickly'; in 快…了, 'about to'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 小晴，快看里面！这不是我的箱子！
examples.trans: Qing, look inside quickly! This is not my case!

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ men. First-person plural pronoun; add 的 for 'our' (我们的).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

meanings.note: Pinyin: biǎn dòu. Literally 扁 ('flat') + 豆 ('bean/legume'), used for flat-podded beans and lentils.

examples.text: 加了柠檬和橄榄油的金黄扁豆汤又香又暖胃。
examples.trans: Golden lentil soup with lemon and olive oil is fragrant and warming.

examples.text: 小美前一天晚上先把扁豆洗干净泡好。
examples.trans: Mei washed and soaked the lentils the night before.

meanings.en: measure word for handled objects; disposal marker
meanings.note: Pinyin: bǎ. Counts items with handles or backs (一把钥匙, 一把椅子); as a preposition, fronts a definite object before an action verb.

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房今天到。
examples.trans: Right, eight guest rooms, eight brass keys. Room four arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tà dǐ. Combines 挞 ('tart') + 底 ('base/crust').

examples.text: 用烤香的杏仁粉做的挞底既酥脆又香甜。
examples.trans: A tart crust made with toasted almond flour is crisp and fragrant.

examples.text: 把挞底烤成金黄色以后，再填入柠檬酱。
examples.trans: Bake the tart shell until golden, then fill it with lemon curd.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhāi. Used for picking herbs, fruit, or flowers, and also for taking off glasses or hats.

examples.text: 这碗番茄汤里放了刚从院子里摘的新鲜香草。
examples.trans: This bowl of tomato soup has fresh herbs just picked from the courtyard.

examples.text: 宋老师摘下眼镜，轻轻合上了那本旧登记本。
examples.trans: Teacher Song took off her glasses and gently closed the old guest book.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīn xiān. Describes fresh fruit, fresh juice, or fresh herbs.

examples.text: 好。端上去之前，在上面撒这些新鲜绿香草。
examples.trans: Good. Before serving them, sprinkle these fresh green herbs on top.

examples.text: 闻闻看！热面包、热炒蛋，还有新鲜香草。
examples.trans: Smell that! Warm bread, hot scrambled eggs, and fresh herbs.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wú dí. Literally 无 ('without') + 敌 ('match/rival'); lively spoken praise for great food or skill.

examples.text: 酥脆的杏仁挞底配上新鲜柠檬，味道简直无敌了！
examples.trans: Crisp almond crust paired with fresh lemon is simply unbeatable!

examples.text: 小美烤的热面包在整条梧桐巷都是无敌的。
examples.trans: Mei's warm baked bread is unbeatable on all of Wutong Lane.

meanings.note: Pinyin: míng tiān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 明天一天 ('all day tomorrow').

examples.text: 欢迎来到小院客栈，小晴。明天不会无聊了。
examples.trans: Welcome to Courtyard Inn, Qing. Tomorrow will not be boring.

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī sān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 这星期三 ('this Wednesday').

examples.text: 等等——星期三晚上你又用真名住进来了？
examples.trans: Wait—and Wednesday night you checked in here under your real name?

examples.text: 每到星期三下午，小美都会试烤新甜点。
examples.trans: Every Wednesday afternoon, Mei test-bakes a new pastry.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī liù. Literally 'week-day six'; Mainland standard alongside informal 周六 (zhōu liù).

examples.text: 每个星期六早上，这条老街都有热闹的集市。
examples.trans: Every Saturday morning, this old street hosts a lively market.

examples.text: 星期六下午来院子里喝杯热柠檬茶吧。
examples.trans: Come to the courtyard for a cup of hot lemon tea on Saturday afternoon.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì. Links two nouns (我是小晴); do NOT use simple 是 before plain adjectives like 好 or 忙.

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
examples.trans: Fair enough! Are these the keys?

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì bú shì. A-not-A affirmative-negative question tag; bù shifts to bú before 4th-tone shì.

examples.text: 我们俩是不是刚升职当上正式试吃员了？
examples.trans: Did the two of us just get promoted to official taste testers?

examples.text: 你是不是把绿色登记本夹在胳膊底下了？
examples.trans: Didn't you tuck the green guest book under your arm?

meanings.note: Pinyin: qíng tiān. Combines 晴 ('clear/sunny sky') + 天 ('day/weather').

examples.text: 姑姑把乐谱收进琴盖里，等着晴天再拿出来弹。
examples.trans: My aunt tucked the score inside the piano lid, waiting for sunny weather to play it again.

examples.text: 大家都盼着明天是个大晴天，好把油漆晒干。
examples.trans: Everyone is hoping tomorrow is a bright sunny day so the paint can dry.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuì. Superlative adverb placed before adjectives or feeling verbs (最好 'best', 最喜欢 'like best').

examples.text: 只有裙子、乐谱，还有我最喜欢的茶杯！
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite teacup!

examples.text: 最上面架子上金色包装那包。怎么了？
examples.trans: The gold-wrapped packet on the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Pinyin: xìng rén. Combines 杏 ('apricot/almond') + 仁 ('nut kernel').

examples.text: 小美端来了一盘刚出炉的温热杏仁饼干。
examples.trans: Mei brought over a plate of warm almond biscuits fresh from the oven.

examples.text: 用杏仁粉做的柠檬挞底吃起来特别香酥。
examples.trans: A lemon tart crust made with ground almonds tastes wonderfully crisp and nutty.

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng méng. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个柠檬 ('a lemon').

examples.text: 他爷爷会切热柠檬蛋糕，上面撒一层白糖粉！
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with a dusting of powdered sugar on top!

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng méng tà. Combines 柠檬 ('lemon') + 挞 ('tart', phonetic loan from English 'tart').

examples.text: 星期二我们要修好琴键，还要烤星期三的柠檬挞！
examples.trans: On Tuesday we will fix the piano key and bake Wednesday's lemon tarts!

examples.text: 酸甜清香的杏仁柠檬挞成了咖啡角的招牌甜点。
examples.trans: Sweet-tart, fragrant almond lemon tart became the café corner's signature dessert.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bàng. Warm colloquial adjective for praising food, work, or ideas (太棒了！).

examples.text: 等等，咸黄油配果酱不行，做炒蛋却棒极了！
examples.trans: Wait—salted butter fails with jam, yet for scrambled eggs it is amazing!

examples.text: 太棒了！用钢笔把你的名字正式写进老陈的大纸本子里！
examples.trans: Wonderful! Your name goes into Chen's big paper ledger in fountain-pen ink!

meanings.note: Pinyin: gǎn lǎn yóu. Combines 橄榄 ('olive') + 油 ('oil').

examples.text: 在热扁豆汤里滴几滴橄榄油，味道更香醇。
examples.trans: Adding a few drops of olive oil to hot lentil soup makes it even richer.

examples.text: 小美用橄榄油和新鲜香草烤了一盘番茄。
examples.trans: Mei roasted a tray of tomatoes with olive oil and fresh herbs.

款.gloss: measure word for menu items, styles, or models

meanings.en: measure word for menu items, styles, or models
meanings.note: Pinyin: kuǎn. Classifier for curated varieties, dishes, cakes, or product designs (一款特色蛋糕 'one signature cake').

examples.text: 每一家街坊咖啡馆都需要一款拿手的特色蛋糕。
examples.trans: Every neighborhood café needs one signature specialty cake.

examples.text: 这两款热茶都很适合搭配杏仁饼干。
examples.trans: Both of these hot teas pair wonderfully with almond biscuits.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhèng shì. Describes formal speech or a permanent job after probation.

examples.text: 我一紧张，句子就变得又长又正式！
examples.trans: Whenever I get nervous, my sentences turn long and formal!

examples.text: 周经理，要是你不正式聘用她，我就请她进我厨房！
examples.trans: Manager Zhou, if you do not hire her permanently, I am hiring her into my kitchen!

meanings.note: Pinyin: měi. Usually followed by a measure word (每个星期 'every week', 每位客人 'every guest').

examples.text: 每个蓝杯子旁边放一张餐巾和一把小勺子。
examples.trans: Beside every blue cup, put one napkin and one small spoon.

examples.text: 老房子每到星期二就松一颗螺丝。坐吧。
examples.trans: Every Tuesday an old house loosens one screw. Sit down.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tāng. Measure word (量词): 碗 (wǎn), e.g. 一碗汤 ('a bowl of soup').

examples.text: 先生，给您干毛巾擦外套，还有一碗热汤。
examples.trans: Sir, here is a dry towel to wipe your coat, plus a bowl of hot soup.

examples.text: 热汤？在冷站台吹了风，喝碗热汤太好了。
examples.trans: Hot soup? After the cold wind on the station platform, hot soup sounds wonderful.

related.gloss: a bowl of soup (measure word 碗)

meanings.note: Pinyin: yóu qī. Measure word (量词): 桶, e.g. 一桶油漆 ('a bucket of paint').

examples.text: 一到七号钥匙全拿走了，八号房刚刷了油漆。
examples.trans: Every key from one to seven is taken, and room eight just got fresh paint.

examples.text: 木门上的蓝油漆还是去年新刷的。
examples.trans: The blue paint on the wooden door was freshly brushed on last year.

related.gloss: a bucket of paint (measure word 桶)

meanings.note: Pinyin: nóng yù. Describes rich soups, coffee, tea, or floral fragrance.

examples.text: 这碗烤番茄汤味道浓郁，配脆皮面包太合适了。
examples.trans: This bowl of roasted tomato soup is rich and full-bodied, ideal with crusty bread.

examples.text: 早晨的咖啡角飘着浓郁的热咖啡香气。
examples.trans: Rich aroma of hot coffee drifts through the café corner in the morning.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wēn nuǎn. Warmer and more emotional than plain 暖; used for sunshine, sound, and kindness.

examples.text: 听……有点低，很温暖，等等——中间这个琴键没有声音！
examples.trans: Listen... a little low, very warm, and wait—this middle key makes no sound!

examples.text: 谢谢你，你的话让我很温暖。
examples.trans: Thank you, your words make me feel warm inside.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kǎo. Used for baking bread, rolls, and cakes in an oven.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

examples.text: 多烤几块边角，好姑娘！
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, dear girl!

meanings.note: Pinyin: rè. Describes hot tea, hot water, or warm weather.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

片.gloss: measure word for slices, leaves, tablets

meanings.en: measure word for slices, leaves, tablets
meanings.note: Pinyin: piàn. Counts thin, flat slices of bread, lemon, cheese, or leaves (一片面包 'a slice of bread').

examples.text: 请给我不加糖的红茶，再来一片热面包。
examples.trans: Black tea without added sugar, please, and one slice of warm bread.

examples.text: 他在红茶里放了一片新鲜柠檬。
examples.trans: He put a slice of fresh lemon into his black tea.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tè sè. Combines 特 ('special/distinctive') + 色 ('character/quality'), common on café and restaurant menus.

examples.text: 杏仁柠檬挞成了小美咖啡角的特色蛋糕。
examples.trans: Almond lemon tart became the signature pastry of Mei's café corner.

examples.text: 这家成都老茶馆很有川西小院的特色。
examples.trans: This old Chengdu teahouse has the distinctive charm of a western Sichuan courtyard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiàn zài. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 现在这时候 ('this moment right now').

examples.text: 现在他的箱子还安全锁着呢。
examples.trans: For now, his suitcase stays safely locked up.

examples.text: 太好了！现在我想吃一顿丰盛的早餐。
examples.trans: Wonderful! Now I would like to eat a big breakfast.

related.gloss: this moment right now (measure word 个)

meanings.note: Pinyin: liú. Used for leaving a note/keepsake, saving food, or staying on (留下来).

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 为什么把鞋和木头小火车留到星期五呢？
examples.trans: Why leave the shoes and little wooden train here until Friday?

meanings.note: Pinyin: fān qié. Standard word for tomato across southern/southwest China (including Chengdu) and menus nationwide.

examples.text: 左边这勺是配了新鲜香草的热烤番茄汤。
examples.trans: This left spoonful is hot roasted tomato soup with fresh herbs.

examples.text: 夏天集市上的熟番茄又红又甜。
examples.trans: Ripe tomatoes at the summer market are bright red and sweet.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Links modifiers or owners to nouns (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǎn. Measure word (量词): 只 (zhǐ), e.g. 一只碗 ('a bowl').

examples.text: 先生，给您干毛巾擦外套，还有一碗热汤。
examples.trans: Sir, here is a dry towel to wipe your coat, plus a bowl of hot soup.

examples.text: 热汤？在冷站台吹了风，喝碗热汤太好了。
examples.trans: Hot soup? After the cold wind on the station platform, hot soup sounds wonderful.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chuāng bǎn. Measure word (量词): 扇 (shàn), e.g. 一扇窗板 ('a shutter').

examples.text: 外面的窗板都关着，所以在院子里谁也没发现！
examples.trans: The shutters outside are all closed, so nobody in the courtyard ever noticed!

examples.text: 还有六天：擦玻璃，刷窗板，烤柠檬蛋糕！
examples.trans: Six days left: clean the glass, paint the shutters, bake lemon cake!

meanings.note: Pinyin: duān. Specifically describes carrying dishes, soup, or tea level in the hands.

examples.text: 好。端上去之前，在上面撒这些新鲜绿香草。
examples.trans: Good. Before serving them, sprinkle these fresh green herbs on top.

examples.text: 她端着一盘热面包走出来。
examples.trans: She walked out carrying a tray of warm bread.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎn dān. Everyday adjective for straightforward tasks.

examples.text: 挺起肩膀，志豪先生。记住那三句简单的话——我去开门！
examples.trans: Shoulders back, Mr Zhihao. Remember those three simple lines—I will open the gate!

examples.text: 这道炒蛋做法很简单，味道却极好。
examples.trans: This scrambled-egg recipe is simple, yet tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎn zhí. Emphatic adverb expressing enthusiastic amazement (简直无敌了 'simply unbeatable!').

examples.text: 杏仁挞底配上新鲜柠檬，味道简直无敌了！
examples.trans: Almond crust paired with fresh lemon is simply unbeatable!

examples.text: 擦亮玻璃后的阳光房简直像变了一间新屋子。
examples.trans: With the glass polished bright, the sunroom looks practically like a brand-new room.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gěi. As main verb, 'give'; as preposition/complement, marks the recipient (给你 'for/to you', 递给我 'pass to me').

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Pinyin: néng. Expresses practical ability or whether circumstances allow something (能睡个好觉).

examples.text: 来成都的第一个晚上，怎么能难过呢！
examples.trans: On your very first evening in Chengdu, how could you sit around sad!

examples.text: 今晚我应该能睡个好觉了。
examples.trans: Tonight I should be able to sleep well after all.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cuì pí. Combines 脆 ('crisp/crunchy') + 皮 ('crust/skin'), especially for artisanal bread (脆皮面包 'crusty bread').

examples.text: 下雨的下午，一碗浓番茄汤配热脆皮面包最舒服了。
examples.trans: On a rainy afternoon, a bowl of rich tomato soup with warm crusty bread is pure comfort.

examples.text: 刚烤好的法式脆皮面包一掰开就咔嚓响。
examples.trans: Freshly baked crusty bread crackles crisp when broken open.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chá. Measure word (量词): 杯 (bēi), e.g. 一杯茶 ('a cup of tea').

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 先喝杯热茶，吃个肉桂卷坐十分钟吧！
examples.trans: Have a cup of hot tea and a cinnamon roll for ten minutes first!

related.gloss: a cup of tea (measure word 杯)

meanings.note: Pinyin: cài dān. Combines 菜 ('dishes/courses') + 单 ('list/sheet').

examples.text: 星期三咖啡角的开业菜单已经全部定好了！
examples.trans: Wednesday's opening menu for the café corner is all set!

examples.text: 小美用漂亮的手写字把今日菜单抄在木牌上。
examples.trans: Mei copied today's menu onto the wooden board in neat handwriting.

meanings.note: Pinyin: báo. Colloquially read 2nd-tone báo when standalone ('thin cup/paper', opposite of 厚 hòu); literary compounds often use bó.

examples.text: 这种薄玻璃杯盛冰柠檬水最好看。
examples.trans: This kind of thin glass cup looks prettiest filled with iced lemon water.

examples.text: 春天的早晚还有点凉，别只穿一件薄外套。
examples.trans: Spring mornings and evenings are still chilly—don't wear just a thin jacket.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dàn gāo. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块蛋糕 ('a piece of cake').

examples.text: 他爷爷会切热柠檬蛋糕，上面撒一层白糖粉！
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with a dusting of powdered sugar on top!

examples.text: 十一点二十分。小美，蛋糕好了吗？
examples.trans: Eleven twenty. Mei, is the cake ready?

related.gloss: a piece of cake (measure word 块)

meanings.en: neighbors; folks on the same street
meanings.note: Pinyin: jiē fang. Measure word (量词): 位 (wèi), e.g. 一位街坊 ('a neighborhood resident').

examples.text: 超过八十年的小院建筑，只要一楼每天服务街坊邻居，禁止改成私人办公室。
examples.trans: Any courtyard building over eighty years old may not become private offices as long as the ground floor serves neighbours daily.

examples.text: 每天服务街坊邻居——就像对公众开放的早间咖啡馆？！
examples.trans: Serves neighbours daily—like a morning café open to the public?!

meanings.en: want; need; will / be going to
meanings.note: Pinyin: yào. Direct verb for ordering/requesting ('want'), obligation ('need to'), or imminent future (要下雨了).

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiàn. Appears in farewells (再见, 明天见) and as result complement of perception (看见, 听见).

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

examples.text: 老陈，听得见吗？我刚经过绿药店！
examples.trans: Chen, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì chī yuán. Combines 试吃 ('sample/taste-test food') + playful role suffix 员 ('official member').

examples.text: 志豪和志鹏笑着宣布他们当上了咖啡角的正式试吃员。
examples.trans: Hao and Peng joked that they had been appointed official taste testers for the café corner.

examples.text: 当小美厨房的试吃员真是全客栈最幸福的工作！
examples.trans: Being a taste tester in Mei's kitchen really is the happiest job in the whole inn!

meanings.note: Pinyin: hái. Everyday adverb meaning 'still' (还在), 'not yet' (还没), or 'even more' after 比.

examples.text: 还没有吗？请记下我们客栈的电话和地址，谢谢！
examples.trans: Not yet? Please write down our inn's phone number and address, thank you!

examples.text: 宋老师，真对不起，那边还没有消息。
examples.trans: Teacher Song, I am truly sorry; they have no news over there yet.

meanings.en: and also; in addition; still have
meanings.note: Pinyin: hái yǒu. Adds another item to a list ('plus…').

examples.text: 只有裙子、乐谱，还有我最喜欢的茶杯！
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite teacup!

examples.text: 两双棕色大男鞋，还有灰色毛衣。
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes, plus grey sweaters.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhè. Proximal demonstrative; pairs with a measure word before nouns (这个 'this one', 这间房 'this room').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà. Distal demonstrative before measure words (那个 'that one'); at clause start, means 'then / well then'.

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dōu. Summarizes everything BEFORE it and always stands directly before the verb/adjective (我们都喜欢).

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: pèi. Used for pairing foods together or cutting spare keys.

examples.text: 咸黄油能配甜草莓果酱吗？
examples.trans: Can salted butter go with sweet strawberry jam?

examples.text: 等等，咸黄油配果酱不行，做炒蛋却棒极了！
examples.trans: Wait—salted butter fails with jam, yet for scrambled eggs it is amazing!

meanings.note: Pinyin: sū pí. Combines 酥 ('flaky/crisp') + 皮 ('pastry crust').

examples.text: 左边这片柠檬挞用的是薄酥皮，右边用的是杏仁挞底。
examples.trans: The lemon tart slice on the left uses thin flaky pastry; the right uses an almond crust.

examples.text: 刚出炉的苹果派酥皮金黄松脆，香气扑鼻。
examples.trans: Fresh from the oven, the apple pie's flaky pastry is golden, crisp, and fragrant.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǐ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 里面 ('the inside').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

meanings.note: Pinyin: jīn huáng. Praises freshly baked pastry crusts.

examples.text: 正在架子上放凉呢——金黄外皮配甜柠檬糖霜！
examples.trans: Cooling on the rack right now—golden crust with sweet lemon glaze!

examples.text: 刚烤出来的面包卷外皮一片金黄。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls came out golden-brown.

meanings.note: Pinyin: suǒ. Works as both verb ('lock the door' 锁门) and noun ('a lock' 一把锁).

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yuàn zi. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个院子 ('a courtyard').

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

examples.text: 朝院子，就在老树上面，非常安静。
examples.trans: Toward the courtyard, right above the old tree; it is very quiet.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jí shì. Traditional open-air neighbourhood or farmers' market (星期六集市 'Saturday market').

examples.text: 星期六一早，小晴和小美提着竹篮去逛集市。
examples.trans: First thing Saturday morning, Qing and Mei carry bamboo baskets to browse the street market.

examples.text: 集市上的本地蜂蜜和黄柠檬比超市新鲜多了。
examples.trans: Local honey and yellow lemons at the street market are much fresher than in supermarkets.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xū yào. Polite everyday verb and noun ('need').

examples.text: 太好了。请告诉我需要知道什么。
examples.trans: Great. Please tell me what I need to know.

examples.text: 凉？啊——对！老街水管早上需要慢慢热身！
examples.trans: Cool? Ah—yes! Old-street water pipes need a gentle morning warm-up!

meanings.note: Pinyin: miàn bāo. Measure word (量词): 片 (piàn), e.g. 一片面包 ('a slice of bread').

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 闻闻看！热面包、热炒蛋，还有新鲜香草。
examples.trans: Smell that! Warm bread, hot scrambled eggs, and fresh herbs.

related.gloss: a slice of bread (measure word 片)

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiāng cǎo. Measure word (量词): 盆, e.g. 一盆香草 ('a pot of herbs').

examples.text: 好。端上去之前，在上面撒这些新鲜绿香草。
examples.trans: Good. Before serving them, sprinkle these fresh green herbs on top.

examples.text: 老陈，这些香草是你自己种的吗？
examples.trans: Chen, did you grow these herbs yourself?

related.gloss: a pot of herbs (measure word 盆)
